column1: # What a percentage height resolves against when a ratio settles the parent.
# Measured on Chrome Headless Shell 153.0.8010.12, the chromium Playwright pins here.

column4: note
control -- the ratio settles the box itself, and already did
the defect: a whole-height child of a ratio-sized parent
the same, proportional rather than whole
out of flow under the same parent
control -- a declared height wins and the ratio does not fight it
the other axis: height declared, width derived
a minimum resolves against it too
and a maximum, which is the third kind build drops
neither axis declared -- the width is shrink-to-fit and it still resolves
the width is itself a percentage, and the ratio still settles the height
control -- without the ratio the parent settles nothing
block-level, no width stated -- the width is the containing block and the height is derived from it
two ratios deep, the outer measured -- shrink-to-fit around a ratio box
the same tree, the inner measured -- does the outer ratio change what the inner derives
a ratio item in a column flex container -- the width is the cross axis and stretches
a ratio item in a grid track -- the width comes from the track
an author min-height beside a ratio on a shrink-to-fit width -- the larger floor wins
half the height of a shrink-to-fit ratio parent, where the whole-height row is the KNOWN one
shrink-to-fit ratio box whose content exceeds the derived height -- does the width follow
the issue shape itself: a plain 30x10 child under ratio .85 on a shrink-to-fit parent
a shrink-to-fit ratio child inside a ratio parent whose width is declared -- the parent is not entangled
content one pixel short of the derived height -- the derived one should win and the width should not move
content one pixel past it -- if the width moves here and not above, the threshold is the derived height itself
a ratio above 1 with short content, so a direction rule cannot be an artefact of the ratio side of 1
a definite width well above ratio 3, where the derived height was wrong by a factor rather than absent
the same at a ratio far enough that the box rendered nothing at all, which a wrong size is not
the same ratio with content past the derived height
the same box clipped -- if the automatic minimum is what makes 300, this is 118
overflow: scroll -- does it drop the automatic minimum the way hidden does
overflow: auto -- does it drop the automatic minimum the way hidden does
clipped and carrying an author min-height -- the explicit minimum survives and takes the width with it
content taller than the ratio implies -- decides whether a derived height is a floor, a ceiling or an override
